text:
The Rangers arrive in Calgary two days after a 3-1 loss at Edmonton that ended their three-game winning streak, even though they held 65% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) that night. They are 3-2-0 in their last five and are missing Alberts Smits and Sean Durzi. Braden Schneider has moved in beside Pettersson and is up to 20:23 a night from 18:11 since Durzi went out, and Adam Fox is up to 24:42 from 22:46. The Flames come off a 4-3 overtime win over Philadelphia, won by Matt Coronato, but they are 2-2-1 in their last five and are without Kevin Bahl, Connor Zary and Samuel Honzek.

New York has controlled more of the play at five on five (53% of the expected goals to Calgary's 47%), and Calgary takes 4.2 penalties a game against a Rangers power play that creates 0.72 expected goals a night. Our model has it 3.07 to 2.78 for the Rangers. In net, projected starter Joonas Korpisalo (one start this season, -0.15 goals saved above expected) is a question mark against Devin Cooley, projected for Calgary, who has 2.38 goals saved above expected this year after 17.23 last season and is 5-0-0 in his last five starts.

For the Rangers, we like Pavel Dorofeyev (31% to score) and Alexis Lafrenière (30%), whom ESPN credited with the NHL-leading 7th goal on Nov. 8. For Calgary, Joel Farabee is our top pick at 31%, and Coronato is one goal from 50 career goals.
